about: The original blend of the non-Cuban La Gloria Cubana, the brand the Perez-Carrillo family built in Miami and later sold to General Cigar. It is a medium-bodied Dominican cigar in an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, now sold by Forged Cigar Co.
notes: The maker calls this line Classic; it is the brand's original cigar. 1972 is when the non-Cuban brand began, not a date for the current blend. A Connecticut Broadleaf maduro version is sold as Classic Maduro. Famous Smoke lists it as medium to full.

filler: USA (Connecticut Habano medio tiempo), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Esteli), Honduras (La Entrada)
about: A value-priced La Gloria Cubana built around medio tiempo, the small, strong leaves that grow at the very top of some tobacco plants. Here that leaf is a Connecticut-grown habano used in the filler.
notes: The maker lists the Churchill at 7 1/4 x 54; halfwheel's launch story printed 7 1/2 x 54.

about: La Gloria Cubana's big ring gauge line, known for thick sizes and a fuller, spicier take on the brand's Dominican and Nicaraguan blend. It is one of the cigars credited with starting the large ring gauge trend.
notes: Most sizes also come in a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro. Serie R Esteli and Serie R Black are separate blends. The maker calls it medium to full; Famous Smoke calls it full-bodied.
verifyNotes: Filled released as 1999 from a 2013 General Cigar press release on halfwheel, which also backs the large ring gauge claim. Swapped one halfwheel source for that page. Blend, sizes and strength match the maker.

about: A darker, bolder companion to Serie R, with a very dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It came out in 2010 and is no longer on the maker's list.
notes: Neptune lists Dominican Republic and full strength; Holt's lists Nicaragua, a Nicaraguan wrapper and medium-full. General Cigar said in 2013 that no La Gloria Cubana had been made in Nicaragua before then, which supports Dominican Republic. A fourth size, Rojo (6 1/2 inches), also existed but its ring gauge could not be confirmed.
verifyNotes: Country kept as Dominican Republic: Neptune says so and a 2013 General Cigar press release rules out Nicaragua for a 2010 line. Replaced the Holt's source link with that press release and reworded notes. No field values changed.

about: A La Gloria Cubana blend created by Michael Giannini, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, a Connecticut Habano binder and extra ligero from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua in the filler.
notes: Not on the maker's current list. Famous Smoke still sells it; Neptune shows it as no longer available. Both list it as full strength, though Famous also describes the blend as medium-bodied. Neptune lists the No. 13 at 5 1/2 x 54.
verifyNotes: Removed cocoa and leather from flavors: the Famous Smoke pages only say sweet, spicy, creamy and peppery. Release year not found, left null.

about: A La Gloria Cubana made at the STG Esteli factory in Nicaragua and named for that city. It pairs a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper with Honduran binder and filler, so it is not a Nicaraguan puro.
notes: Not the same as Serie R Esteli, which is a separate, older blend.
verifyNotes: Rewrote about. The claim that it was the first La Gloria Cubana named for the city where it is rolled is not supported: Serie R Esteli and Serie R Black were announced as Nicaraguan-made in 2013.

filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Dominican Republic (Olor, Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa)
about: A box-pressed La Gloria Cubana named for the Spanish press method, where cigars go into divided trays right after rolling to set their shape. The blend uses tobacco from four countries under a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper.
notes: The maker describes it as medium-bodied; Famous Smoke lists it as full.

about: A limited edition shaped by votes from more than 2,000 members of the La Gloria Cubana Society, the brand's online fan group. The first release in 2022 was a Honduran puro; a second, different blend followed in 2023.
notes: Blend shown is the 2022 release (2,500 boxes of 20). The 2023 Society Cigar II is a different blend: Honduran Habano wrapper, Ecuadorian Sumatra binder, Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, with earth, leather, hazelnut and coffee notes.

about: A La Gloria Cubana made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr., whose family owned the brand until 1999, at his own factory in the Dominican Republic. Each cigar carries a second band with his name.
notes: Made at Perez-Carrillo's factory, not at General Cigar Dominicana like most La Gloria Cubana lines.

about: A La Gloria Cubana made exclusively for Famous Smoke Shop, introduced at the store's Cigarnival event in 2013. It wraps Nicaraguan filler and a Honduran binder in a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra Oscuro leaf.
notes: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. Sizes are the ones Famous sells now; the 2013 launch sizes were different (5 x 52, 6 x 54, 6 1/8 x 60, 7 x 52). Famous lists it as medium, though it launched as a stronger take on the regular line.
verifyNotes: Removed the note that Neptune lists a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran filler: the Neptune page would not load, so it could not be confirmed. Country and strength rest on Famous Smoke alone.

about: La Palina's everyday, value-priced line. The original 2012 Classic had a Brazilian wrapper and was made at PDR Cigars; since the 2017 revamp the base blend is sold as Classic Natural with a Honduran wrapper, alongside Connecticut, Maduro and Rosado versions.
notes: Now sold as Classic Natural. Blend shown is the maker's listing; halfwheel reports a Honduran binder and adds Honduran filler, and lists the Robusto at 5 1/2 x 50. First reported as made at General Cigar Dominicana, later at STG Danli in Honduras.
verifyNotes: Dropped Neptune from the Robusto size note, as its Classic Natural page was not opened. 2012 launch, Brazilian wrapper and PDR Cigars confirmed on halfwheel.

about: The Connecticut shade version of La Palina's value-priced Classic line, introduced with the 2017 revamp. An Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper covers a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
notes: Neptune lists strength as medium and describes it as mild to medium-bodied. First reported as made at General Cigar Dominicana; halfwheel later reported the Classic lines are made at STG Danli in Honduras.
verifyNotes: Reworded about to remove sales language. Strength comes from Neptune only; the maker gives no strength word.

about: The maduro version of La Palina's value-priced Classic line, with a dark Honduran wrapper and binder over Dominican, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
notes: This is the 2017 blend. An earlier La Palina Maduro from 2012 had a Mexican wrapper and is a different cigar. First reported as made at General Cigar Dominicana; halfwheel later reported the Classic lines are made at STG Danli in Honduras.
verifyNotes: Removed the claim that it is the boldest of the Classic blends, which no source states.

about: The dark, full-strength member of La Palina's Label Series, launched in 2014. The maker says it is loaded with Central American ligero.
notes: Sources disagree on the blend and where it is made. The maker lists Habano Maduro over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The 2014 original was made at PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic with a Brazilian wrapper. Neptune still shows the Brazilian blend but names Honduras and Plasencia, and lists the Gordo at 6 x 58.
verifyNotes: Blanked country (was Honduras). The maker does not state it, halfwheel's 2014 review says Dominican Republic, and the only page saying Honduras (Neptune) also calls it a cigar from the Dominican Republic. Rewrote about: no source says it was the company's strongest cigar. Wrapper and strength confirmed.

about: A member of La Palina's Label Series built for flavor instead of strength. It starts mild and creamy and settles at medium, with plenty of spice.
notes: Launched in 2015 from PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in four sizes; Neptune lists the later version as made by Plasencia in Honduras. Neptune marks every size discontinued and the maker's main product list no longer shows it. Neptune also listed a 6 x 60 Gordo.
verifyNotes: No changes. Country rests on Neptune alone, since halfwheel only covers the 2015 Dominican-made launch version. Confirmed the maker's product list has Red Label commented out.

about: A La Palina Label Series cigar that began in 2018 as a single toro for Tobacconists' Association of America shops and went nationwide in three sizes in 2019. It is made in Danli, Honduras.
notes: Wrapper is disputed: the maker lists Ecuador (Sumatra), halfwheel reported Ecuadorian habano in 2018 and Honduran habano in 2019, and Neptune's spec says Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed while its description says dark Habano. The maker calls it medium to full-bodied; Neptune lists medium.
verifyNotes: Corrected the note about Neptune: its spec table lists an Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed wrapper, in line with the maker. No field values changed.

about: A collaboration between La Palina and Rocky Patel, made at Plasencia's El Paraiso factory in Honduras. It started in 2017 as a single toro for Tobacconists' Association of America shops and became a regular line in 2018.
notes: Wrapper is disputed: the maker lists Ecuador (Habano), while halfwheel and Neptune list a Honduran wrapper. halfwheel listed the Robusto at 5 1/2 x 50; the maker and Neptune list 5 x 50. A 4 x 54 Bullet was a limited size. Each cigar is aged at least six months in cedar rooms.

about: A limited series named for founder Sam Paley's wife, Goldie Drell, and rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana. The blend includes medio tiempo leaf, each cigar has a fan-tail cap, and new sizes come out in small runs.
notes: Every size is a limited run in boxes of 10, usually one or two new releases a year. Until she retired in 2017 every Goldie was rolled by Maria Sierra, who once rolled Cohibas in Havana. Sizes are from halfwheel's release list; the maker's page gives different measurements for two of them.
verifyNotes: Reworded about to drop 'top limited cigar'. Strength comes from Neptune only; the maker gives no strength word.

about: La Palina's early everyday cigar; the name is Spanish for 'the daily'. It was made in Honduras with a Honduran corojo wrapper, a double Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler, and the small KB (Kill Bill) size began as part of this line.
notes: Not on the maker's product list and no longer sold at Neptune, but halfwheel still named an El Diario series in a March 2023 La Palina price notice. The same blend is sold as the KB Series. Neptune's spec says medium and its description says medium to full; the maker called the KB size full bodied. Other sizes existed but were not confirmed.
verifyNotes: Removed Toro 6 x 50 and Gordo 6 x 58: no page opened lists them, only the Robusto. Filled released as 2011 from halfwheel. Changed production from discontinued to null, since halfwheel listed an El Diario series in a March 2023 price notice. Swapped one Neptune link for the halfwheel 2011 page.

about: The dark-wrapper half of La Palina's two Nicaragua lines. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a habano oscuro wrapper, medium to full in body.
notes: Reblended in 2023 when production moved to Joya de Nicaragua. The 2016 original was made by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian oscuro wrapper.
verifyNotes: Removed the note about Neptune's listing, which was not a listed source and could not be opened. No field values changed.

about: The light-wrapper half of La Palina's two Nicaragua lines. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Nicaragua, light to medium in body and creamy.
notes: Reblended in 2023 when production moved to Joya de Nicaragua. The 2016 original was made by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, and Neptune's listing still describes that version and calls it medium.
